transcript: People get real quiet when you start talking about recovery. They love the success story, but they don't like the part where you had to crawl through hell to get there. Let me tell you something. I'm not hiding my story to make anybody comfortable.
I lived addiction. I lived chaos. I lived jail cells, funerals, and whole nights wondering if I'd wake up. And now that I'm clean, people want me to whisper about it.
Nah, not happening. I'm breaking that stigma every time I speak. Because the truth is, there are people out there dying in silence because they're scared to be judged for healing. Think about that.
People will clown you for getting clean, but stay quiet when you're destroying your life. That's the world we live in. So hear me clearly. You don't owe anyone a pretty recovery.
You don't owe anyone a fake version of your journey to make them feel safe. Your story is real. Your scars are real. Your comeback is real.
And the more you speak up, the more people realize addiction doesn't look one way. It looks like me. It looks like you. It looks like real people who decided they wanted better.
If you're done being silent, if you're done being ashamed of the work you're doing, drop a heart and stand with me. We're breaking this stigma, loud and unfiltered. Let's build something and rise.
